subject: Architecture
title: Lotte World Tower: Seoul's Giant
description: A short lesson to help you apply Lotte World Tower: Seoul's Giant.

hook.text: South Korea's tallest building took 13 years to approve because of fears it would crash into a nearby air base.

buildup.text: At 1,819 feet, Lotte World Tower tapers gently like a traditional Korean ceramic brush.

discovery.text: Its glass floor observation deck hangs 1,600 feet up — the highest glass-bottom floor in the world.

twist.text: The tower houses a concert hall, aquarium, hotel, offices, and apartments — a vertical city in one shaft.

climax.text: Seoul's skyline was once limited by airspace rules. Lotte proved supertalls could coexist with flight paths.

punchline.text: Thirteen years of 'no' turned into South Korea's tallest 'yes.'

quiz.question: Why did Lotte World Tower take 13 years to approve?
options: Environmental concerns about the Han River
Fears it would interfere with a nearby air base
Disagreements over the building's design style

details.summary: Lotte World Tower in Seoul, completed in 2017 at 555 meters, features a tapered form inspired by Korean ceramic curves. It houses offices, a hotel, residences, observation decks, and a concert hall, demonstrating the mixed-use trend in contemporary supertall design.
details.whyItMatters: Lotte World Tower shows that supertall buildings can serve entire communities rather than single corporate tenants. Its cultural and residential components make it a vertical city center rather than just an office tower.
takeaways: Completed in 2017 at 555 meters in Seoul, South Korea
Tapered form inspired by Korean ceramic art traditions
Mixed-use program includes offices, hotel, residences, and culture

faq.question: Why is Lotte World Tower tapered?
faq.answer: The gentle taper references the elegant curves of traditional Korean celadon pottery. Structurally, tapering reduces wind loads at the top and concentrates mass at the base, improving stability. The form achieves cultural expression and engineering efficiency simultaneously.

faq.question: What can visitors do inside Lotte World Tower?
faq.answer: The building contains a shopping mall, offices, a luxury hotel, residential apartments, a concert hall, an observation deck with a glass-floor section at 500 meters, and South Korea's highest swimming pool. It functions as a self-contained vertical city.
